label: Example quarterly IRRBB run
note: A run plan is data. It is authored by a person or an agent, diffed against the last approved plan, and validated by the type gate and the routing gate before anything executes. Nothing in this file is a result. The graph also RUNS: the behavioral stages form a chain that rewrites the book one licensed binding set at a time, the contractual pass reads the last link, and the metrics read the series. Two stages, st-client-rate and st-draw, name catalog components no mounted plugin executes (the engine mounts a flat-carry client-rate plugin under its own name, engine.behavioral.loan-client-rate, not under the catalog component st-client-rate names): they compile to not-implemented tags because no type only they produce is read by another stage, and either would refuse the plan outright the moment a metric consumed it.

stages.note: The all-in funding curve, its own contract type. EVE discounting must state whether it runs the all-in or the risk-free leg, because the two are not comparable, so the two legs are two types: st-curve produces ZeroCurve and this stage produces FundingCurve. A metric that needs both names both producers, and a metric that names neither is refused at the gate. The day count is the one the engine executes; a curve stage that declares another is refused at the gate.

The deterministic shocked path the default profile mounts. A stochastic term structure, alm-hull-white among them, is a plugin a profile mounts in this row's place: the plan names the component, and a component no mounted plugin declares is refused rather than silently skipped.

The first link of the behavioral chain: it reads the context book and hands the rewritten book to the next link. Tier 1 on a $1.0B book because the long-dated option makes EVE sensitive per dollar, not because the balance is large.
Same component, narrower selector, lower order. The personal and auto books carry less option content than the mortgage book.

A catalog entry awaiting an executor: the engine mounts a flat-carry client-rate plugin under its own name (engine.behavioral.loan-client-rate), not under this catalog component, so this stage still compiles to a not-implemented tag and nothing reads its path. It sits OFF the behavioral chain, because a stage nothing executes may not be a link in a chain the numbers flow through.

A catalog entry awaiting an executor: the engine mounts no draw-rate plugin, so this stage compiles to a not-implemented tag. It is the binding liquidity model on the thinnest-data row of the map, carried as a management assumption because the utilization data will not support a stable fit, and the only behavioral family in the catalog with a forward model and no calibration component.

Deliberately does not feed NII. The going-concern earnings run takes its balance from the new-volume stage, and routing decay into NII is the canonical routing error the gate exists to catch. The selector's dimensions predicate names the calibration segments the decay bindings may cover; a decay binding on a position outside those segments is refused at compile by L1.

The engine's deposit-beta overlay rewrites the position's repricing terms like every other behavioral kind, so this stage produces a Position and not a rate path. DepositRatePath stays in the contract vocabulary for a future rate-side model that genuinely produces one.

The last link of the chain: the contractual pass runs on the book this stage hands over. Carried as a management assumption despite adequate materiality and data, because the driver test overrides the quadrant: brokered rollover is a funding-mix decision, so the history records treasury strategy rather than depositor behavior.

Builds the contractual stream for every position of the effective book the behavioral chain produced. It no longer claims a commitment schedule: the contractual pass does not produce one, and T6 refuses a claim an executor cannot keep.
The stage that owns the NII balance. A static scenario gets its contractual series back unchanged; a dynamic one is reinvested. The engine's balance-plan stage carries this stage kind.

The optional metric. A plan that omits it gets a result with no ftp block, which the result contract has permitted since 1.2.0; a plan that names it gets the three-leg par-match for the base scenario.

reports.note: How much EVE sits behind a Tier 1 model versus a management assumption.

typeGate: T1 Every stage's consumed types are produced by a declared upstream stage or supplied by a context file.
T2 Unit and sign conventions agree across every edge, per the contract plane.
T3 The as-of date and grid are consistent across all stages.
T4 The dependency graph is acyclic and every dependsOn resolves.
T5 No stage is orphaned: everything is reachable from an input and reaches a metric.
routingGate: R1 For each behavioral stage, every metric in feeds[] must be non-none for that stage's behavioral class in the routing policy.
R2 A stage whose declared disposition is M may not be routed to a metric the policy marks A, without a documented override.

R3 Every selector must match at least one position in the book, so a binding cannot silently apply to nothing. Behavioral selectors bind on behavioralClasses, the multi-valued dimension, because one balance can be governed by more than one behavioral model.
R4 Every position carrying a behavioral class must be matched by at least one behavioral stage, so a material book cannot silently run contractual-only.
